content.title: Build a reusable panel
Why composition beats configuration sometimes
content.text:
A common temptation is to create a component with twenty props:

```jsx
<Card
  title="..."
  showTitle
  titleSize="large"
  body="..."
  footer="..."
  showFooter
  footerMode="button"
  // ...
/>
```

Sometimes a simpler composition API is clearer:

```jsx
<Card>
  <Header />
  <Body />
  <Footer />
</Card>
```

The right answer depends on the component's job, but composition is often the better escape hatch when the contents vary.

feedback.correct: The second component owns the container behavior without owning the exact content.
feedback.incorrect: The second component owns the container behavior without owning the exact content.

content.title: Senior insight
content.text:
A good abstraction often answers this question:

**What should this component own, and what should the parent still be free to choose?**

That question is more useful than “How many props should this component have?”

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Composition lets a component provide structure while the parent provides content.
**Senior habit:** When a reusable component starts growing lots of “showX”, “variantY”, and “modeZ” props, ask whether composition would make the boundary simpler.
